blocks.explanation: Equation for measuring economy-wide price inflation.

blocks.title: First-Principles Core Truth
blocks.summary: Real GDP adjusts nominal output for inflation using constant base year prices, while the GDP Deflator measures economy-wide price changes across all domestic output.

blocks.content: 1. Nominal GDP ($GDP_{\text{current}}$): Total output valued at current prevailing market prices ($P_{\text{current}} \times Q_{\text{current}}$). Affected by volume AND inflation.
2. Real GDP ($GDP_{\text{constant}}$): Total output valued at constant base year prices ($P_{\text{base}} \times Q_{\text{current}}$). Measures actual physical production growth!
3. GDP Deflator: Implicit price deflator measuring overall inflation: $\text{GDP Deflator} = \frac{\text{Nominal GDP}}{\text{Real GDP}} \times 100$.
4. Green GDP: $\text{Green GDP} = \text{Real GDP} - \text{Environmental Degradation Cost} - \text{Natural Resource Depletion Cost}$.

blocks.text: ⚡ 1. Nominal GDP vs. Real GDP Matrix

rows: Constant base year prices ($P_0$, currently 2011-12 in India)
High (can increase even if physical output falls!)
Zero (reflects purely physical volume changes $\Delta Q$)
Standard for comparing true economic growth over time

blocks.text: 📖 2. GDP Deflator vs. Consumer Price Index (CPI)

rows: ALL domestically produced goods and services
Fixed basket of consumer goods and services
**INCLUDED** if consumed by households (e.g. imported edible oil)
Dynamic / Paasche index (weights change with output composition)

items: **Concept:** Standard GDP treats natural resource depletion as income rather than capital loss. Green GDP adjusts standard GDP for environmental externalities.
**Global Framework:** UN **System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA)** framework.

blocks.content: ⚠️ **Exam Trap 1:** If Nominal GDP grows by 10% and Inflation is 4%, Real GDP growth is approximately **6%** ($10% - 4%$). Nominal growth alone does NOT mean physical output expanded by 10%!
⚠️ **Exam Trap 2:** GDP Deflator includes capital goods (machinery) and government services, whereas CPI includes only consumer goods.

#### Tier 1 — Recall MCQ
**Q:** Why is the GDP Deflator considered a broader measure of economy-wide inflation than the Consumer Price Index (CPI)?  
(A) It includes imported consumer goods  
(B) It covers all domestically produced goods and services including capital goods  
(C) It uses a fixed basket of goods from 2004  
(D) It is published weekly by RBI  
**Answer: — GDP Deflator reflects prices of all domestic output, not just household consumer items.

#### Tier 2 — Applied Scenario
**Scenario:** In FY26, India's Nominal GDP is ₹300 Lakh Crore, and Real GDP (at 2011-12 base prices) is ₹180 Lakh Crore. Calculate the GDP Deflator.  
**Resolution:**  
$$\text{GDP Deflator} = \frac{300}{180} \times 100 = 1.6667 \times 100 = \mathbf{166.67}$$  
(This indicates price levels have risen by **66.67%** relative to the 2011-12 base year).

#### Tier 3 — Mains Descriptive Prompt
*'Distinguish between Real GDP, Nominal GDP, and Green GDP. Why does standard GDP fail to reflect sustainable development, and how does Green GDP address this limitation?'*

🎯 Exam Angle → 🔥 HIGH — National Income Invariant: National Income in India is officially defined as **NNP at Factor Cost** ((	ext{NNP}_{	ext{FC}})). Formula: (	ext{GVA}_{	ext{Basic Prices}} = 	ext{GDP}_{	ext{MP}} - 	ext{Product Taxes} + 	ext{Product Subsidies}).
